title: Are robot vacuums enough? Where automation fails
excerpt: Robot vacuums offer convenience, but they have significant limitations. Find out where automation falls short and whether a robot vacuum is enough for you.

blocks.text: Why waste time cleaning when you can hire a robot to do it for you? That's the logic that makes robot vacuums attractive to many homeowners. However, there are limitations to robot vacuums that are important to consider when comparing a robot to a regular vacuum.

So, are robot vacuums worth it? Or are they more of a gimmick than a revolutionary home cleaning solution? This article will cover everything you need to know about the pros and cons of robot vacuums to help you decide if one is worth investing in.
The attractiveness of robot vacuum cleaners

It's not hard to see why robotic vacuum cleaners have become so popular. They automate a task that otherwise requires time and physical effort, while also looking modern and futuristic. This appeal has made robotic vacuum cleaners one of the fastest-growing categories of home appliances. However, widespread adoption doesn't automatically mean they're suitable for every household.
Why smart home automation is so appealing

For homeowners investing in smart home technology, a robot vacuum cleaner seems like the next step. Features like app-controlled scheduling, voice assistant integration, and room mapping technology make these devices look truly futuristic. The combination of practicality and futuristic appeal is what makes all of smart home automation appealing, and robot vacuums are no exception.
The convenience factor that drives adoption

Robotic vacuum cleaners operate autonomously, often while homeowners are away, and return to their places when they're done. There's no doubt that this level of convenience is appealing. The question is, are robotic vacuum cleaners replacing regular vacuums or are they more suitable as a practical addition to your cleaning routine?
Understanding the advantages and disadvantages of a robotic vacuum cleaner

On the plus side, robotic vacuums offer consistent daily maintenance, hands-free operation, and compatibility with smart home platforms. On the minus side, they have significant limitations in suction power, debris removal capacity, floor coverage, and access to above-floor areas.
Where Robot Vacuums Struggle
Robotic vacuum cleaners work best in a narrow range of conditions. If you go outside those conditions, performance quickly declines.
Can robot vacuums clean carpets well?

On hard floors and low-pile carpets, robot vacuums work relatively well. On deeper carpets, they struggle. Most robot models generate significantly less suction and brush movement than full-size vacuums, making it difficult for them to effectively clean medium- and high-pile carpets.
Limitations of high-pile carpets and deep pile
Many robot vacuums struggle to navigate through thick carpet fibers, and their brushes often lack the torque needed to lift embedded material from the carpet.
Why corners, edges and moldings are often missed
The circular shape of most robot vacuums creates a geometric problem: corners and tight edges remain inaccessible no matter how sophisticated the vacuum's navigation system.
Cleaning stairs, upholstered furniture and gaps above the floor

No robot vacuum cleaner invented so far is capable of climbing stairs or cleaning upholstered furniture. Any furniture or surface that is not a wide, flat surface will still require a traditional vacuum cleaner to clean.
Battery life, dust capacity and maintenance requirements

Most robot vacuums have small dust bins that require frequent emptying. Battery life also limits run time. While much of the maintenance required by a robot vacuum is common to upright vacuums, robot vacuums introduce additional maintenance needs, such as keeping the sensors clean and functioning.
When automation creates a false sense of cleanliness
A floor swept by a robot vacuum cleaner may look clean, but it actually isn't. Here's why automation sometimes creates this ''false sense of cleanliness'':
Surface collection vs. deep cleaning performance

There's an important difference between a floor that looks clean and a floor that's been thoroughly cleaned. Robot vacuums excel at the former. They pick up visible surface debris, pet hair, and crumbs. What they don't do is pull out the small particles, compacted debris, and ground-in dirt that accumulate in carpet fibers and floor joints over time. This means that a deep-cleaning robot vacuum is likely to give unsatisfactory results.
Why a broom doesn't replace deep extraction

Frequent light cleaning maintains appearance, but is not a substitute for periodic deep cleaning. High-traffic areas, carpeted areas, and homes with pets or children accumulate debris that surface cleaning cannot remove.
Common problems with robot vacuum cleaners - from their users

In addition to performance limitations, owners often report navigation errors, tangled brushes, missed areas, and stuck appliances. These problems with robot vacuums are exacerbated when they operate unattended, meaning families may not discover missed floors until a buildup of debris becomes apparent.
Are robot vacuums enough for the whole house?

For whole-house cleaning, robot vacuums tend to fall short. They can't clean stairs, upholstered furniture, higher surfaces, or deep-seated carpet residue. Instead, they're better used as a supplement to your cleaning routine, not as a primary solution.
Robot vacuum cleaner vs. regular vacuum cleaner

Comparing a regular vacuum cleaner to the best robot vacuum cleaner is ultimately a comparison between two different categories of tools. One automates routine maintenance; the other provides the power and versatility needed to thoroughly clean your entire home. Understanding where each is better makes it easier to use both effectively.
Differences in Airflow, Motor Power, and Agitation

Full-size upright vacuums are equipped with significantly larger motors that generate much more airflow and suction. The brushes in full-size appliances also allow for deeper shaking of carpets. Systems like the Kirby Avalir Platinum use high-performance motors, specifically designed to remove debris from carpets, not just hard surfaces.
Manual control vs. automated navigation

Automated navigation offers convenience, but sacrifices the control and adaptability of manual cleaning. A robotic vacuum cleaner follows programmed patterns; a person using a full-sized vacuum cleaner reacts to what they see. Areas with a lot of debris, visible buildup, and problem spots receive focused attention during manual cleaning that automated systems cannot replicate.
Deep cleaning option vs. maintenance

Robotic vacuums are great at maintenance, while full-size vacuums are great at deep cleaning. Both serve legitimate purposes and can complement each other well. A heavy-duty vacuum provides the suction, attachments, and mechanical power needed for deep cleaning. A robot prevents that work from piling up too quickly between sessions.
What to consider before replacing your primary vacuum cleaner

Robotic vacuums work best when used in conjunction with full-size vacuums, not as a replacement. Before you decide to replace your primary vacuum with a robotic unit, there are a few important factors to consider:
How often do you do a deep cleaning

If you frequently deep clean your home, using a robot vacuum for deep cleaning will not yield the same results. The best approach is to routinely deep clean your home with a reliable vacuum, then use a robot vacuum for maintenance between sessions.
Your floor type and household waste load

Households with hard floors and no carpeting represent the best-case scenario for robot vacuums. Meanwhile, homes with carpeting, households with pets, and homes with small children are much more difficult for a robot vacuum to handle on its own.
Understanding the difference between practicality and capability

Robotic vacuums offer real convenience. They're not just a gimmick, and if you use them properly and understand their limitations, they can be a useful cleaning tool that saves you a lot of time. However, they don't deliver the cleaning capabilities of a full-sized device. Robotic vacuums work best as part of a complete system, not as a replacement for one. Systems like Kirby offer add-ons that expand their cleaning capacity to every floor in the home, filling in the gaps left by automation. For homeowners who are ready to invest in a long-term solution, Kirby backs its systems with a comprehensive warranty and a history built on decades of whole-home cleaning.

title: Homes with multiple types of floors need different types of vacuum cleaners
excerpt: Homes with different floors offer unique cleaning challenges. Learn why a single-use vacuum isn't enough and how to choose a machine that can handle different floor types.

blocks.text: The reality of different floors in modern homes

Homes rarely feature just one type of flooring. Most often, some combination of hardwood, tile, carpet, and rugs cover the floors of a home, and sometimes even in the same room. This creates a cleaning environment that no single-purpose vacuum cleaner can handle well.
Why Hardwood, Tile, Carpets, and Rugs Require Different Cleaning Approaches

Each surface has its own unique cleaning requirements. For example, hardwood and tile floors are not tolerant of aggressive brushes. At high speeds, brushes tend to scatter fine debris rather than pick it up, and the stiff bristles can scratch such floors over time. Carpet, on the other hand, requires agitation to pick up embedded particles. Rugs are a special category, often requiring both deep agitation to pick up debris and reduced suction to prevent the rug from lifting. These varied cleaning requirements make a quality vacuum cleaner essential for homes with a variety of flooring types.
How design trends have changed household cleaning needs

Open floor plans, popular in both new construction and renovated homes, combine multiple flooring types into one continuous space. When a vacuum can move from hardwood to large carpet or tile in a single pass through the living and dining room, a multi-floor vacuum makes the most sense.
Why disposable vacuum cleaners aren't enough

Most vacuum cleaners are designed around one type of surface. That design focus produces strong results under the right conditions, but leads to problems the moment the machine encounters a different material.
When a carpet-only vacuum struggles on hard floors

Vacuum cleaners optimized for carpets rely on aggressive agitation and high airflow. However, on hard floors like tile and hardwood, these settings tend to blow fine particles outward, rather than pulling them in. That's why the best vacuum cleaner for hardwood tile and carpet is one that can adjust the agitation and airflow settings.
Why hard floor settings may not work well on carpet

The reverse problem is equally common. A vacuum designed to glide smoothly over tile or hardwood floors doesn't have the proper brush height and agitation needed to reach the carpet fibers. It tends to pass over embedded debris, rather than extracting it.
The frustration of switching between multiple machines

Many families with different floors buy separate machines for each type of surface. The problem is that this approach increases equipment costs, requires additional storage, and adds time to each cleaning session. A true multi-surface vacuum eliminates this.
What makes the right vacuum cleaner different

A multi-floor vacuum cleaner is not just a general-purpose machine. Instead, it is a vacuum cleaner that can adjust its settings from one surface to another without sacrificing cleaning quality on any surface.
Adjustable height and surface-specific contact

The defining feature of the best multi-floor vacuum cleaner is its adjustable height. A height-adjustable vacuum cleaner allows you to adjust the distance between the vacuum head and the floor to optimize brush roll contact for each floor type.
Airflow control and suction regulation

A vacuum cleaner for hardwood and carpet requires suction that adjusts to the resistance of the surface. Hardwood and tile offer little resistance to airflow, so excessive suction creates drag, making it difficult to push the vacuum cleaner and potentially pulling lightweight carpets off the floor. Carpet, on the other hand, requires more suction to pull debris up through the fibers. For a multi-floor home, you need a vacuum that adjusts suction based on the type of floor.
Agitator and Protection Brush Design

The best vacuum for homes with mixed floors should have brushes that are designed for multi-surface performance and protection. That means the bristles are stiff enough to loosen carpet fibers, soft enough to avoid scratching wood, and spaced so that debris is directed toward the vacuum, rather than scattered. Multi-surface vacuums address this challenge with a brush that has softer outer bristles for surface contact and tougher inner bristles for penetrating the fibers.
Sealed systems that maintain consistent performance

Loss of suction tissue through poorly sealed housings affects performance on any surface, but the impact is most obvious on hard floors, where debris scattering is immediately visible. A reliable multi-floor vacuum with sealed filtration and an airflow system maintains consistent suction across a variety of floor types.
How to effectively vacuum different types of floors
Even with a multi-surface vacuum cleaner, each surface still requires a unique cleaning approach. Adjusting the cleaning method for each surface will yield much better results.
Best Practices for Hardwood and Tile

Slow passes are the best way to clean hard floors, as fine particles require constant contact with the suction power to be collected. On tiles, pay special attention to the grout lines, which tend to trap small debris.
Carpet cleaning without causing lifting or damage

Even the best vacuum cleaner for carpets and hardwood floors can sometimes struggle to clean carpets. Vacuuming hard enough to clean the lint also lifts the carpet itself, slowing you down and potentially damaging the carpet. Reducing the suction or raising the vacuum head before going over the carpet, then returning the settings once it's centered on the lint, will help prevent this.
Seamless transition between carpet and hard floors

Transitioning between different surfaces is where single-purpose vacuums have the biggest problems. Debris accumulates at the edges of the floor because a vacuum calibrated for one surface scatters or ignores what it encounters at the boundary. Adjusting the height settings before each pass ensures that the machine will work well on both surfaces.
Signs that your vacuum cleaner is not designed for different floors

It's not always obvious that a vacuum cleaner isn't working well on different types of floors. If you're not sure how well your machine is cleaning your multi-surface home, there are a few signs you can look for.
Uneven collection of waste across surfaces
If a vacuum cleaner works well on carpet but leaves visible residue on hardwood, or vice versa, it's a strong sign that the machine is designed for one surface and not the other.
Excessive scattering on hard floors
If fine particles are visibly scattered in front of or next to the vacuum head on tile or hardwood, the brush roll speed or suction calibration is not matched to that surface.
Carpet edge sticking or surface resistance

If your vacuum cleaner gets caught on the edges of carpets or encounters resistance on surfaces, the solution is a vacuum cleaner for carpets and hardwood floors that includes settings optimized for both sides.
Special tools are needed for daily cleaning

It can be a hassle when a standard cleaning session requires you to switch between multiple tools to clean your home. A heavy-duty vacuum cleaner built for mixed floors allows you to clean your entire home with one machine, and accessories let you expand its capabilities even further.
Why mixed-use homes benefit from a systems approach

Cleaning a home with multiple floor types doesn't have to mean owning multiple machines or accepting inconsistent results. The right vacuum cleaner works as a unified system, adapting to each surface, rather than requiring you to adjust your expectations.
A machine designed to adapt to changing surfaces

A multi-year vacuum cleaner allows you to eliminate the hassle of constantly changing machines without compromising performance on the different surfaces in your home. With a vacuum cleaner like the Kirby Avalir Platinum that offers adjustable height, regulated suction, and an adjustable brush, you can effectively clean hardwood, tile, carpet, and rugs with one machine.

title: Are you still using the same vacuum cleaner for 10 years?
excerpt: A high-powered vacuum cleaner can often last for years. However, just because a vacuum cleaner is still working doesn't mean it's working properly. Here are 5 tests to determine if it's time for a new one.

blocks.text: A high-powered vacuum cleaner can often last for years. However, just because a vacuum cleaner is still working doesn't always mean it's working properly. Old vacuum cleaner problems, such as poor suction, tend to become more common as equipment ages and components wear out.
To help you decide if it's time to replace your vacuum, here's a Kirby upgrade guide that covers the signs you need a new one.
Why does vacuum cleaner performance change over time

Vacuum cleaners have many moving parts, and every piece of equipment with moving parts wears out over time. As components like the motor, belts, airflow systems, and brushes age, the overall performance of the system can gradually decline.
How daily use affects suction and cleaning power

Every vacuum cleaner experiences wear and tear during operation. From minor motor wear that reduces suction power, to belt stretching that reduces brush performance, to the gradual clogging of filters and airflow channels, many problems can occur during normal, everyday use. These changes can occur slowly, making them difficult to notice until cleaning performance begins to decline.
The difference between ''still working'' and ''still sucking''

A vacuum cleaner that turns on and picks up visible debris may seem to be functioning normally. However, performance involves more than just basic operation. If your vacuum cleaner doesn't provide consistent suction across surfaces, requires multiple passes to clean a particular area, or vibrates excessively, it may be time to replace it, even if it's technically still working.
Test 1: Checking the consistency of suction

Perhaps the simplest vacuum cleaner performance test is the suction consistency test. This test allows you to see what kind of suction your vacuum cleaner provides on different surfaces and is a great way to check if everything is working properly.
How to identify suction loss

Start by vacuuming a small area of the carpet or floor where there is visible debris. Observe how quickly the vacuum picks up the debris.

Signs of loss of suction include:
- Debris remaining after one pass
- Dirt is being blown away instead of being picked up
- Reduced airflow at the hose or attachment
Repeat the test on different surfaces in your home. If the vacuum requires multiple passes to pick up debris that previously went away quickly, there is likely a loss of suction power.
Comparison of carpet and hard floor vacuuming performance

A well-performing vacuum cleaner should be able to switch between surfaces without a dramatic change in performance. Test the vacuum on both carpet and hard floors. If it picks up debris easily on one surface and not the other, the cause may be airflow restriction or brush wear.
Multiple passes
Occasional extra passes are needed during intensive cleaning, but if your vacuum cleaner is constantly requiring multiple passes to clean a particular area, its performance is likely reduced.
Test 2: Residue Retention Test

A vacuum's internal airflow system plays a big role in how well it works. Bags, filters, and internal passages help collect debris while also allowing air to move freely through the machine.

Here's a vacuum performance test you can use to make sure this system is working properly:
Inspection of bags, filters and air flow system

Start by checking to see if your vacuum cleaner bag or dust container is full. Overfilled bags can reduce airflow and limit suction. Next, inspect the filters and internal system for signs of blockage or debris retention. If there is excessive buildup, airflow may be restricted. This not only reduces suction, but can also cause the motor to work harder than necessary, further accelerating wear.
Signs of blockage or reduced air circulation

Along with a visual inspection, other signs of blockage or reduced airflow include:
- Reduced suction at the floor head
- Warm air coming out of the exhaust system
- Noticeable debris buildup inside the machine
If you notice any of these signs, cleaning the airflow system may improve performance.
How maintenance affects the overall result

Routine maintenance often prolongs the performance of a vacuum cleaner's internal airflow system. By replacing bags, cleaning filters, and checking the airflow system, you can avoid many of the problems that cause a vacuum cleaner to degrade in performance.
Test 3: Noise and Vibration Assessment
Unusual noise or vibrations often signal internal problems. On the vacuum cleaner upgrade checklist, a strange, constant noise is pretty high on the list.
Unusual sounds that may indicate full usage

Listen for changes such as:
- Cracking or knocking sounds
- Higher-pitched engine noise
- Sudden increase in volume
Problems such as worn bearings or unbalanced brushes are often the cause of these unusual sounds.
How engine load affects long-term reliability

When components wear out or airflow becomes restricted, it often causes the vacuum cleaner motor to take on extra strain. Stressing the motor can lead to reduced suction, increased heat generation, and faster wear. If noise or vibration continues after routine maintenance, the vacuum cleaner motor may be nearing the end of its service life.
Test 4: Overview of Add-ons

If you're asking yourself, ''Is it time to replace my vacuum cleaner?'', you need to consider more than just the vacuum cleaner itself. The accessories are also important and should function as intended.
Are the tools still working as intended?
Connections should connect securely and provide consistent suction. Make sure all accessories fit tightly into the hose, maintain suction during use, and operate without air leaks.
How accessories affect whole-home cleaning

Accessories extend the reach of a vacuum cleaner and allow it to handle different surfaces. When your vacuum cleaner can easily adapt to different cleaning needs, it indirectly improves performance. That's why it's important to test your accessories as part of your vacuum cleaner upgrade checklist.
When outdated plugins limit performance

If you're having problems with a single accessory, you may be able to restore performance by replacing just that accessory, rather than the entire vacuum cleaner. However, if multiple accessories are failing, it's probably a sign that your entire system is about to break down.
Test 5: Maintenance and Repair
The final test includes an evaluation of the vacuum cleaner's maintenance history. This vacuum cleaner maintenance test can help you decide whether to repair or replace your vacuum cleaner.
Tracking repairs, parts replacements and downtime

Consider the following questions:
- How often have you had to replace parts in recent years?
- Does the vacuum cleaner often lose performance after short periods of use?
- Have repairs become more frequent over time?
If you have made many repairs or are having frequent problems, the vacuum cleaner may be nearing the end of its optimal performance period.
When ongoing maintenance signals it might be time for a replacement

A vacuum cleaner that requires constant maintenance or replacement of parts not only reduces performance, but also becomes a hassle and expense. In these cases, replacing the vacuum cleaner is often more economical than constant maintenance.
Understanding the difference between a repair and an upgrade

You don't always have to replace your vacuum cleaner at the first sign of trouble; repairs can often restore it to optimal performance. When the system itself begins to show consistent decline, instead of a single, replaceable part, upgrading to a new, more reliable vacuum cleaner is a better choice.
What the results mean for your cleaning routine

After completing these five tests, you should have a pretty clear picture of how well your vacuum is performing and whether it's time for an upgrade. If you're noticing any performance issues or problems with your old vacuum, it's likely affecting your cleaning routine.
When poor performance means an upgrade

When your vacuum cleaner isn't working properly, you waste time on extra passes and your cleaning routine becomes less efficient. It also increases the likelihood of frequent repairs that can be costly. That's why noticeable differences in performance often justify an upgrade. By replacing your old vacuum cleaner with a high-quality model like the Kirby Avalir Platinum Vacuum Cleaner, you can optimize your cleaning routine and say goodbye to frequent repairs.

title: Why do vacuum cleaners break down so quickly and how to break the cycle
excerpt: Cheap vacuum cleaners are intentionally designed to be replaced every 2-3 years. Understanding this problem can help you avoid that cycle of constant replacement.

blocks.text: Most people expect a new vacuum cleaner to last for years. However, a surprisingly large number of vacuum cleaners start showing problems much sooner than expected. Problems with cheap vacuum cleaners, such as reduced suction, frequent clogging, and mechanical failures, are common when you buy a machine that isn't built to last, and these problems often show up much sooner than they should.

Understanding the causes of vacuum cleaner lifespan problems is the biggest key to avoiding them. To help you extend the life of your vacuum cleaner, here's everything you need to know about why vacuum cleaners break down, along with maintenance tips to keep your vacuum cleaner running well for as long as possible.
Ending the ''replacement every two years'' scheme
Vacuum cleaner lifespan issues have become a common frustration. However, many are surprised to learn that this is not entirely accidental. In some cases, it is intentional.
Why many families feel stuck in the replacement cycle

Cheap vacuum cleaners aren't built to last. In fact, they're intentionally designed to be replaced every two to three years so the company can keep selling new vacuums to its customers. The reason many homeowners feel stuck in the cycle of replacement is simple: that cycle is by design.
What a longer-lasting vacuum cleaner can change

A vacuum cleaner built for long-term use changes this equation. When the machine maintains consistent suction, supports regular maintenance, and provides access to replacement parts, it can last a lifetime, rather than having to be replaced before the color even starts to fade.
The frustration of disposable vacuum cleaner design

Many modern home appliances emphasize lightweight design and lower initial costs. While these features make the products easier to manufacture and cheaper to buy, they are also the main reason why appliances no longer last as long as they used to.
Problems with a cheap vacuum cleaner that appear during the first year

Problems with cheap vacuum cleaners often appear quickly. Common early warning signs include:

- Reduced suction power
- Inconsistent vacuuming performance
- Increased noise during operation
- Belts and brushes wear out quickly

These problems may start as minor annoyances, but often become more noticeable over time.
Performance degradation and inconsistent suction

Decreasing suction power is one of the most common complaints associated with old vacuum cleaners. When airflow is restricted or motors lose efficiency, the vacuum cleaner can't vacuum as well as it did when it was new. This problem leads to longer cleaning sessions and repeated passes over the same areas.
When repairs cost almost as much as replacement

Cheap vacuum cleaners are designed to be replaced, not repaired. Parts are often hard to find, and even when you do find the one you need, repairing the vacuum cleaner can cost as much as buying a new model. In these cases, repairing the vacuum cleaner versus replacing it becomes the obvious choice, creating a cycle of constant replacement that frustrates many families.
How common breakdowns affect cleaning habits

When a vacuum cleaner is prone to malfunctions and breakdowns, it can directly affect cleaning habits. Families may be reluctant to use the machine unless they absolutely have to. And during times when the vacuum cleaner is down, using it isn't even an option.
Why do vacuum cleaners break down so quickly
There are several factors that contribute to frequent vacuum cleaner failures. While every machine is different, here are some of the common problems that reduce the lifespan of a vacuum cleaner:
Lightweight materials and engine limitations

Many vacuum cleaners prioritize lightweight construction and low manufacturing costs. While these features make the machines easier to manufacture and transport, they can also limit their long-term durability.
Overheating, clogging and neglect of maintenance

Maintenance plays a significant role in the lifespan of a vacuum cleaner. Overfilled bags, blocked airflow channels, and neglected filters can force motors to work harder than intended, reducing their lifespan.
Short product life cycles and rapid model change

Many cheap vacuum cleaners are designed to be replaced every time a new model comes out. This means that many vacuum cleaner failures are designed to occur quickly, as a result of the rapid change of models.
Vacuum cleaner lifespan issues related to design compromises
Compromises in design often determine how long a vacuum cleaner remains reliable. Machines designed primarily for a low initial cost sacrifice durability, repairability, and long-term support.
What changes with a permanent system
Not all vacuum cleaners follow the disposable design model. When you buy a heavy-duty vacuum that's built to last, you can avoid the cycle of replacement.
Durable construction built for long-lasting use

Reliable, well-made vacuum cleaners feature a sturdier construction and stronger internal components. This allows them to maintain consistent performance over years of use and avoid frequent breakdowns.
Reconstructive components instead of disposable parts
Another big difference is component replacement. Instead of throwing away the entire machine when a part breaks, rebuildable systems allow for the replacement of individual components.
Access to spare parts and service support

One of the key factors for long-term reliability to consider is the availability of replacement parts and service support. When parts and service for a vacuum cleaner are readily available, problems can be resolved quickly, rather than requiring you to purchase a new machine. That's why Kirby provides a complete catalog of replacement parts and accessories for all of its models.
A guarantee that supports ownership

Warranty also plays an important role in long-term vacuum ownership. A strong warranty not only means that repair costs will be covered, but it also signals that the manufacturer is confident in the durability of its product.
How to extend the life of your vacuum cleaner, no matter what you own

Even with a durable machine, proper maintenance remains essential to extend the life of your vacuum cleaner. Here are some vacuum cleaner maintenance tips to keep your vacuum cleaner performing optimally:
Routine vacuum cleaner maintenance tips that prevent early system failure

Some of the most important maintenance practices to extend the life of your vacuum cleaner include:

- Replace bags before they become full
- Check filters regularly
- Check airflow tubes
- Check belts and brushes

These steps help maintain airflow and reduce stress on internal components.
When to repair vs. replace

The decision between repair and replacement often comes down to the condition of the vacuum cleaner and the availability of parts. If one component fails and replacement parts are readily available, repairing the vacuum cleaner is the best option. However, when multiple components start to fail at the same time, it's probably better to buy a new machine.
Why the right settings and plugins are important

Vacuum cleaner settings and accessories also affect long-term performance. Using the correct height adjustment and accessories ensures that the vacuum cleaner operates under the conditions for which it was designed.
Choosing a vacuum cleaner made to break the cycle of replacement
If you're frustrated by the constant cycle of buying a new vacuum every time your old one breaks, buying a durable, high-quality vacuum like a Kirby is the key to breaking the cycle.
Why durable vacuum cleaners change long-term costs

A cheap vacuum cleaner isn't really that cheap if you're forced to buy a new one every few years. Well-made vacuum cleaners that are built to last may cost more upfront, but the long-term costs are often much lower.
How Kirby vacuum cleaner durability supports years of use
Kirby vacuums are designed with durability, rebuildable components, and long-term service support in mind. These features help owners maintain performance for years.
A smarter investment in home cleaning equipment

A high-quality vacuum cleaner is a long-term investment. With the right system and consistent maintenance, the cycle of frequent vacuum replacement is broken, allowing you to make a one-time investment in a machine that lasts longer and performs better than cheap, low-quality alternatives.

title: Does wireless convenience cost you more? What low-battery models won't tell you
excerpt: Cordless vacuum cleaners have become popular thanks to their mobility and modern design, but their practicality is much less than advertised.

blocks.text: Cordless vacuums have become a hot new product in the cleaning industry, and it's easy to see why. Between their sleek designs, lightweight frames, and easy portability, there's a lot to like about them compared to their corded equivalents.

However, the comparison of normal vacuum cleaners versus cordless ones does not end there. While the benefits are clear, there are also some disadvantages of cordless vacuum cleaners that need to be taken into account.
This article will provide a comprehensive overview of the cordless vs. cordless vacuum debate, looking at key comparisons such as convenience, battery life, suction power, and more.
The appeal of cordless vacuum cleaners

In many ways, cords feel like outdated technology in 2026. Even at first glance, it's easy to see the appeal of cordless vacuums. But here's a closer look at some of the main reasons why customers are drawn to them:
Why wireless designs feel modern and easy to use

''Cordless'' is a popular trend among consumers, and cordless vacuum cleaners fit perfectly into that. They look like something from the future when you see them on the shelves, and that's very important when it comes to consumer demand.
The promise ''right now''

Cordless designs allow you to immediately pick up the vacuum and start cleaning. Although the time it takes to plug in the cord is quite negligible, the idea of ''immediately'' is still very appealing.
How marketing emphasizes freedom over performance
Cordless vacuum cleaner manufacturers emphasize freedom and mobility a lot in their marketing, but don't talk as much about performance. It turns out there's a reason for this...
Explanation 1: ''Wireless is easier to use''

The appeal of cordless vacuums is clear. The problems with cordless vacuums, on the other hand, are usually not apparent until you buy one. That's why it's important to carefully consider the benefits that cordless vacuums claim to offer, starting with the idea that they're easier to use.
Where comfort ends and compromise begins

Cordless vacuums remove the physical tether of a power cord, but they introduce a new dependency: charging. The convenience of ''instant'' cleaning quickly disappears when your vacuum loses power during a cleaning session or refuses to charge when you need it.
Time constraints and work interruptions during cleaning

Most cordless vacuums advertise run times under ideal conditions, often at lower power settings. High-performance modes significantly reduce that run time. These vacuum battery life issues can cause frequent interruptions and impose a time limit on each cleaning session.
Why refill cycles change cleaning habits

Battery dependency reshapes behavior. Families often delay cleaning until the batteries are charged or avoid major cleaning sessions altogether. What starts as a convenience gradually turns into a compromise.
Explanation 2: ''The suction power is basically the same''

Many cordless vacuums promise strong suction, comparable to what you get with a corded model. However, vacuum performance testing doesn't always confirm this, especially when battery drain is taken into account.
How battery drain affects performance over time

Most people assume that cordless vacuums operate at maximum power until their battery is completely drained and empty, but that's not how it actually works. As batteries run low, the motors compensate by reducing power. This results in suction power that gradually decreases throughout the cleaning session.
What a vacuum cleaner performance test often reveals

Vacuum cleaner performance tests side by side often show measurable differences between corded and cordless vacuum cleaners. While cordless models may work well at first, their performance often drops significantly as their batteries drain. In any vacuum cleaner suction power comparison that compares performance over time, corded vacuum cleaners are the clear winner.
Excuse 3: ''Wireless models are lighter and simpler''
The lightweight design of cordless vacuum cleaners is one of their biggest advantages. However, it's an advantage that comes with a few key drawbacks:
Compromise between lightweight design and engine strength
Reducing weight often requires reducing the size of the motor. While lighter vacuums may seem easier to maneuver, this often comes at the expense of suction power and durability.
How design affects deep carpet cleaning
Good carpet cleaning requires a constant flow of air. Lightweight cordless vacuums often have difficulty providing that combination for extended periods, especially as their batteries run low.
When multiple passes replace the efficiency of a single pass

Reduced suction means that cordless vacuums often require multiple cleanings to achieve the same results as corded vacuums. When you have to spend extra time going over the same spot multiple times, it offsets the other benefits that cordless models offer.
Explanation 4: ''Get cheaper''
It's true that, on average, cordless vacuum cleaners have a lower initial price than corded models. However, the initial price is not the only cost to consider.

title: What to do when your vacuum cleaner smells: most common causes and solutions
excerpt: When a vacuum cleaner starts to emit unpleasant odors, it usually indicates accumulated dirt or parts that haven't been cleaned for a long time.

blocks.text: A well-maintained vacuum cleaner should leave your home cleaner — not fill it with unpleasant odors. When your vacuum starts to smell musty or sour, it usually indicates built-up dirt or areas that haven't been cleaned in a while. Over time, these odors can affect the freshness of the air in your home and reduce cleaning efficiency.
What causes the unpleasant odor?
Full bags and accumulated dust over time. When vacuum cleaner bags become full, airflow is reduced and the trapped dirt begins to decompose.
Clogged or dirty filters: Filters that are not cleaned or replaced regularly become a source of unpleasant odors every time you turn on the vacuum cleaner.
Pet Hair, Dirt, and Moisture: Hair and organic materials can begin to decompose and create a sour or musty odor.
How to remove odors
Empty the bag or container regularly and replace filters as recommended. Check brushes, hoses, and internal channels for accumulated debris and moisture.
Safe Deodorization: Use only Kirby-approved products, like Kirby Deodorizer Drops, and avoid homemade mixtures that can damage the system.
Let the vacuum cleaner air out after use and follow regular maintenance instructions to maintain freshness and efficiency.

title: The power of specialized pet hair removal brushes
excerpt: Specialized vacuum cleaner brushes turn pet cleaning into a simple and efficient routine.

blocks.text: Pet ownership brings joy, companionship and, let's face it, a lot of hair. Whether it's shedding season or everyday mess, keeping your home clean can feel like a constant battle. Specialized vacuum cleaner brushes help make this challenge a simple, easy routine by effectively and precisely targeting pet hair, dander and debris.
The Importance of Specialized Brushes

Pet hair tends to find its way into every corner of the home. Regular vacuuming with standard attachments can pick up visible hair, but often fails to pick up hairs that are deeply embedded in carpets and upholstery. Specialized vacuum cleaner brushes solve this problem by more effectively picking up and removing hair, helping to create a fresher, more comfortable indoor environment.

Vacuum cleaner brushes designed for cleaning pet debris use unique bristle configurations and rotating actions to agitate and loosen hair from various surfaces. This design not only improves suction power, but also prevents hair from getting tangled around the rollers, maintaining consistent suction and performance.

When choosing a vacuum cleaner for cleaning pets, consider the following factors:
- Bristles design: Firmer bristles help pull hair out of thick carpet pile.
- Rotation speed: Faster rotating brushes improve agitation and pick up dirt.
- Ease of maintenance: Easy-to-clean brushes prevent clogging and extend their lifespan.
- Compatibility: Make sure the brush fits and works seamlessly with your vacuum model.

Seasonal shedding can leave larger hairballs on carpets and furniture. Specialized brushes are great at removing these things, reducing buildup, and making routine cleaning more efficient. For homes with shedding-prone pets, frequent use of these brushes helps keep surfaces looking and feeling cleaner.
Specialized vacuum cleaner brushes

Vacuum cleaner brushes and similar specialized tools offer several key benefits:
- Improved lint collection: Models are designed specifically for pet hair to prevent re-deposition.
- Improved airflow: Reduced buildup helps maintain strong suction power.
- Targeted cleaning: Ideal for areas with lots of pets, such as upholstery, beds, and carpets.
- Reduced odors: By removing built-in lint and debris, these brushes help spaces stay fresher.
Keeping your home fresh and comfortable

A well-maintained vacuum cleaner, equipped with specialized brushes and pet supplies, is essential for pet owners looking to simplify their cleaning routine. By effectively handling pet hair and dander, these accessories help maintain a fresher, more pleasant environment, even during heavy shedding season.

title: Using HEPA filters to improve air quality through carpet cleaning
excerpt: HEPA filters play an important role in improving indoor air quality by effectively trapping fine particles when cleaning carpets.

blocks.text: Standard vacuum cleaners often only remove visible debris, while releasing smaller particles like dust, pollen, and pet dander back into the environment. These microscopic pollutants can circulate through indoor spaces, reducing overall air quality and freshness. Vacuum cleaners equipped with HEPA filters are most effective at capturing these particles, helping to improve indoor air quality during routine cleaning.
Why indoor air quality matters

Indoor air should reflect the comfort and cleanliness of a space. Since people spend a significant amount of time indoors, maintaining a clean atmosphere is essential for overall comfort and cleanliness.
Contaminants commonly found in carpets

Dust and dirt embedded in carpet fibers accumulate a wide range of particles daily. These contaminants can become lodged deep within the fibers, going unnoticed without regular cleaning. Common contaminants include:

- Dust and dirt
- Pollen and outdoor allergens- 
- Pet hair and dander
- Cooking residue
- Dead skin cells

The types of contaminants vary with seasonal fluctuations. For example, winter often increases indoor dust due to closed windows, while spring brings higher pollen levels.
How carpets affect air circulation

Carpets act as reservoirs for airborne particles circulating throughout the home. Ordinary activities like walking can disrupt the accumulated pollutants, returning them to the air. This ongoing cycle illustrates how carpets affect home air quality.
How carpet cleaning supports air quality

Routine carpet cleaning removes contaminants embedded in carpet fibers. Eliminating these contaminants reduces their recirculation, resulting in a space that feels and smells cleaner. Regular maintenance contributes to an improved indoor atmosphere.
The effect of trapped particles in space

Even when surfaces look spotless, hidden contaminants in carpet fibers can affect the overall freshness and comfort of a room. Removing the smallest particles makes a space feel cleaner, brighter, and less burdened with unwanted odors or residue.
The Importance of Regular Maintenance

Vacuuming two to three times a week with a machine equipped with HEPA filters helps prevent the accumulation and build-up of particles. Establishing a consistent schedule reduces the likelihood that airborne particles will become a problem.
Long-term maintenance and quality of the indoor environment

Continuous carpet maintenance plays a key role in maintaining indoor cleanliness. Regular removal of particles helps preserve both the condition of the carpet and the freshness of the indoor air. Over time, this routine results in a visibly and atmospherically cleaner space.
Why HEPA filters make a difference
HEPA filters retain fine particles that standard filters often miss. They effectively retain dust, pollen, and animal allergens, preventing them from being re-released into the air.
What HEPA technology retains
HEPA filters are designed to capture at least 99.97% of particles as small as 0.3 microns. This includes pollutants smaller than pollen grains, which standard filters cannot effectively capture.
HEPA vs. standard filtration
Standard filtration can be compared to a mesh that stops larger particles, while HEPA filtration functions like a very fine sieve that retains even the smallest dirt.
HEPA certifications and standards
Certified HEPA filters meet strict efficiency standards. Labels like 'True HEPA' confirm that the filter has been tested and verified to retain microscopic particles.
Improving cleaning with HEPA vacuum cleaners
Vacuum cleaners with HEPA filters allow for the simultaneous removal of visible and invisible dirt. They prevent particles from returning to the air and provide a more thorough cleaning.
A dual approach to particle reduction

Effective cleaning involves removing dirt from carpets and retaining particles that have already been vacuumed during cleaning. This approach reduces the constant re-spreading of contaminants throughout the home.
Good Maintenance Practices
Regular cleaning or replacement of HEPA filters, timely replacement of bags, and frequent vacuuming are key to maintaining the efficiency and cleanliness of the space.
Supporting air quality in the long term
In addition to vacuuming, ventilation, humidity control, and regular wiping with damp cloths further contribute to a cleaner and fresher interior space.

title: Seasonal Cleaning Guide: How to Keep a Comfortable Home Year-Round
excerpt: Each season brings different cleaning challenges, and a well-structured seasonal plan helps keep your home tidy and comfortable all year round.

blocks.text: Each season brings a different cleaning challenge, from summer's mowed grass to winter's mess of snow and salt. The Seasonal Cleaning Guide serves as a framework for meeting the needs of your space.

Seasonal cleaning can help you reduce clutter and protect your home's surfaces, no matter what the weather brings. Here, we'll look at why seasonal cleaning is important and give you practical tips you can use to implement year-round cleaning routines to keep your home cozy and comfortable.
Why seasonal cleaning creates a more comfortable home
Different seasons bring different messes, and these changes mean you need to take a dynamic approach to cleaning.
Adapting to weather conditions and household needs

Whether you're battling spring pollen in your home or working to keep leaves off your living room floors, it's crucial to employ a year-round home care routine that takes into account your home's ever-changing needs.
Benefits of Regular Seasonal Maintenance
Waiting until the mess gets too big can make cleaning seem like an impossible mission. A regular winter, spring, summer, and fall cleaning routine can help prevent major cleaning problems.
A systematic approach for easier cleaning

Using a seasonal cleaning guide is an ideal option for keeping your carpets, floors, and the rest of your home in order. Cleaning systems can also help you divide household chores among your family, leaving less of the burden of deep cleaning on your shoulders.
Spring Cleaning
With the snow melting and more sunlight, spring is ideal for starting a new deep cleaning routine.
Deep cleaning after winter

Floor, furniture and hallways. Focus on deep cleaning floors, especially near entryways that may have been repeatedly greeted by heavy winter boots. Refresh chairs and sofas by cleaning upholstered furniture and don't forget to wash throws and blankets.
Clearing out and storing seasonal items
Store away winter gear, such as heavy coats, boots, snow jackets, and snow shovels. Organize storage boxes and throw away unused clothing and items.
Carpet, Curtain and Upholstery Refreshment

Fabrics retain allergens and odors, especially after a winter with closed windows. Wash curtains, clean and air out carpets, and thoroughly clean upholstery, allowing fresh air to circulate freely throughout your home.
Summer cleaning
With kids out of school and guests coming over more often, you'll need a plan for dealing with the dirt and dust that enters your home.
Control of dust, grass and increased movement
Your summer cleaning list should include frequent vacuuming of floors, especially in entryways and hallways.
Cleaning air vents and fans
A thorough cleaning of your fans can help prepare your home for air conditioning use again. Dust ceiling fans and vacuum or replace filters to reduce allergens and your energy bills.
Maintenance of kitchens and utility rooms
Your kitchen and utility rooms will likely see a surge in activity during the summer. Wipe down counters and other surfaces, as well as floors, and empty trash cans regularly.
Autumn cleaning
As the fall chill sets in, it's time to get started on your fall cleaning routine as you and your family will be spending more and more time indoors.
Preparing for the colder months
Fall is the perfect time to deep clean your floors and carpets to remove summer dirt and allergens.
Closet Organization and Seasonal Replacement
Pack away summer clothes, beach towels, etc. to make room for fall clothes and holiday decorations.
Control of autumn leaves and outdoor dirt
Pets' shoes and paws bring leaves into your home during the fall months, and regular sweeping and vacuuming can help prevent debris.
Winter Cleaning
When the coldest temperatures of the year arrive, you'll be spending more time indoors than ever. Follow these winter cleaning tips to keep your home cozy and comfortable.
Focus on entrances and common areas
Salt and snow tend to stick to shoes, so it's best to take extra care of floors near entrances. Disinfect common areas regularly to keep winter bacteria and viruses at bay.
Preventing salt and moisture build-up
To protect floors from salt and moisture, place mats at all entrances and clean them regularly. Use a vacuum cleaner with wet/dry cleaning capabilities to quickly clean up mud or snow messes.
Maintenance of cleaning tools
Cold weather can damage cleaning equipment, so it's important to store vacuum cleaners and other cleaning tools in moisture-free rooms and regularly check filters and accessories.
Creating a routine that fits your home
No two families or homes are the same, and your cleaning schedule should meet your needs.
Division of tasks by weeks, months and seasons

Creating a calendar that includes weekly tasks (like cleaning low-traffic areas) and monthly tasks (like cleaning blinds or organizing your pantry) can help you keep your cleaning schedule organized. Use the seasons as connecting points to remind you to tackle bigger tasks like washing the carpets.
Consistency with the right tools

Your household's needs should determine your cleaning schedule. If you have small children or pets, for example, you may need to vacuum more often. Tailor your year-round home care plan to the characteristics of your home and your family's needs.
One vacuum cleaner for all four seasons

The right cleaning equipment can simplify your cleaning process. Your vacuum should be able to switch between multiple floor types, reach ceilings and tight corners, and handle wet and dry messes. Extension hoses, upholstery cleaners, and HEPA filters can help keep your home cleaning schedule consistent and efficient.
Kirby complete solution for a whole year

At Kirby, our complete cleaning solution supports all aspects of year-round home care. Our systems are designed to meet your cleaning needs while offering power, versatility and reliability. Whether you're looking for tips for spring cleaning or looking for ideas for winter home maintenance, Kirby offers the extras you need to create a clean, comfortable environment for your home.

title: Understanding the suction power of vacuum cleaners
excerpt: Every vacuum cleaner depends on suction power to effectively remove dirt, dust, and allergens. Understanding suction power helps you choose the right machine for your home.

blocks.text: Vacuum cleaners are essential household appliances that make it easy to remove dust, dirt, and allergens. One of the key factors in a vacuum cleaner's performance is suction power, which measures the appliance's ability to pick up and move dirt.
What is suction power and why is it important
Suction power helps you choose a vacuum cleaner with enough power to effectively clean surfaces and remove embedded dirt.
Definition and units of measurement (Air Watts, Water Lift)

Suction power measures a vacuum cleaner's ability to pull air and dirt. The most commonly used measures are air watts and water lift. Air watts shows how effectively a vacuum cleaner converts electrical energy into suction and airflow. Water lift measures how high the motor can lift a given amount of water, which is useful for deep cleaning carpets.
Why suction power is important for removing dirt

Effective dirt removal depends on sufficient suction power to suck particles from the surface and transport them to the bag or canister. Insufficient power can leave dust, allergens, and pet hair behind.
Factors that affect suction power
Power depends on the airflow, dirt transport systems and the motor. A strong motor and optimized system design are key to maximum suction power.
Airflow and dirt transfer
Air flow carries dirt from the surface to the canister. Both suction and flow are important — without sufficient flow, even strong suction power is not enough.
Suction power vs. airflow
On hard floors, airflow is more important, while on carpets, suction power is key. The best vacuum cleaners combine high suction power and optimized airflow.
Technologies that increase suction power and flow
Technologies such as cyclonic separation, multi-stage filtration and optimized brushes increase efficiency. Regulating airflow and auto-sensors help the vacuum cleaner adapt to conditions.
Different types of vacuum cleaners and suction power
Vacuum cleaners come in different styles, and their power depends on the design and size of the motor.
Management vacuum cleaners
They have powerful motors and wide cleaning heads, ideal for carpets and homes with large surfaces. They offer high suction power for deep cleaning.
Stick vacuum cleaners
Light and comfortable, but usually with less power than manual ones. Suitable only for occasional cleaning and smaller areas.
The robot vacuum cleaner
Autonomous solutions for daily maintenance, with moderate suction power for hard floors and low-reach carpets.
Maintaining suction power over time
Regular cleaning of filters, inspection of hoses and brushes, and replacement of bags help maintain high suction power.
Why maintenance is important
Even the most powerful vacuum cleaner will lose effectiveness if it is not maintained regularly. Clean filters and hoses maintain suction power, reduce noise and electricity consumption.
Tips for long-term maintenance
Change the bag more often, clean the filters once a month, check and clean the brushes and hoses, and store the vacuum cleaner in a dry and cool place.
Modern features that improve efficiency
HEPA filters and specialized accessories like edge and upholstery tools increase cleaning efficiency and help achieve a thorough clean.
How to choose a vacuum cleaner based on your suction power needs

The type of flooring and the presence of carpets determine the type of vacuum cleaner that will be most suitable for you. For a combination of hard floors and thick carpets, a multi-purpose machine with strong suction power and good airflow is recommended.
Key specifications for comparison
Check CFM (airflow), water lift, motor power, and air watts to evaluate efficiency. The overall design of the system also plays a role in optimal cleaning.
